config_name: Legion Pro 5 16" WQXGA (Refurb Excellent) — Ryzen 7 8745HX / RTX 5060 8GB, 32GB DDR5, 1TB SSD

specs.display_type: OLED, glossy (WQXGA tier assumed OLED per tested config)
specs.ports: 1x USB4 40Gbps/TB (DP+PD), 2x USB-A 3.2 Gen2, 2x USB-A 3.2 Gen1, HDMI 2.1, 1GbE RJ45, 3.5mm

battery.notes: 80Wh; 'battery life is typical for the class' (Back2Gaming). ~5h light browsing, ~1-1.5h gaming.

price.notes: Regular $3,829; sale $2749 VERIFIED via BBY API 2026-11-24 (sku 20178812).

reviews.quote: It's built well and clean looking, offers solid ergonomics, decent inputs, and a beautiful OLED display that you won't normally find in this segment.
strong raster performance from the RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU, excellent motion clarity from the 240Hz 2560×1600 OLED, and a cooling design that sustains clocks without resorting to gimmicks.
it focuses on nailing the fundamentals: strong performance, a fantastic display, sturdy build quality, and a keyboard that's genuinely comfortable to use.

professional.note: Pro scores are for the tested Ultra 9 275HX / RTX 5070 Ti / 32GB config (NBC collection 86.8%); this tier's ratings inferred per SHARED-legion-pro5.md deltas.

praises: $2,749 CAD refurb (BBY "Excellent") for the Pro 5 chassis + RTX 5060 is one of the best price-per-frame deals in Canada today
Same sturdy Pro 5 chassis, comfortable TrueStrike keyboard, and upgradeable dual SODIMM/dual M.2 as the full-price tiers
RTX 5060 runs cool and quiet in this chassis — the cooling stack is over-spec for this GPU
32GB RAM standard despite the discount price
DLSS 4 frame-gen keeps the 5060 viable at WQXGA in most current titles
complaints: Refurb unit: no first-owner warranty history, possible cosmetic wear; panel type (IPS vs OLED) not guaranteed
Ryzen 7 8745HX has no NPU — Copilot+ features and local-AI acceleration absent
8GB VRAM on the 5060 is the first thing to run out in new AAA at WQXGA max settings
Battery remains mediocre even with the smaller GPU — desk machine
Some Gen 10 Legion 50-series units hit nvlddmkm TDR black-screen crashes (platform-wide Legion reports)

design_philosophy: Lenovo's 'mainstream affordable Legion Pro' bet: take the Pro 7 chassis language, keep the strong 140W-class GPU cooling and comfortable TrueStrike keyboard, and differentiate with an OLED panel rarely seen at this tier — while trimming premium extras (rear I/O, big speaker arrays). This 275HX/5070 Ti/32GB/2TB tier is the sweet-spot config the professional reviewers tested and recommend: standouts = OLED 240Hz + upgradeable RAM/storage; dealbreakers for some = battery life and sale-price-dependent value.
rating_notes: Inferred from anchor 80 per SHARED-legion-pro5.md: RTX 5060 8GB vs 5070 Ti = -2.2 gaming / -0.8 ai_ml; Ryzen 7 8745HX (8c, no NPU) -0.7 productivity; easier GPU/cooling headroom +0.5 thermals / +0.5 battery. Refurb "Excellent" condition at BBY — notable value pick today at $2,749.
